aboutH2: Centre for Wholeness & Well Being: outpatient recovery in SW Calgary
intro: The Centre for Wholeness & Well Being is an outpatient counselling and recovery centre in Calgary's Currie neighbourhood, in the city's southwest. It is not a residential rehab. People come in for appointments and go home afterwards, and the centre says plainly that it does not offer medically supervised withdrawal or 24-hour care. It works out of Brad House, a heritage building at 3911 Trasimene Crescent SW, and is run by a registered charity, the Alberta Association for Better Communities.

Its addiction program is called Empower Recovery. The centre describes it as a non-12-step, non-residential pathway that mixes counselling, recovery coaching and family support, so people can keep working and stay at home while they get help with substance use. It is aimed at people who need more structure than an occasional counselling session, people who have just finished residential treatment, and people who have returned to use and want support quickly. The centre says there is no waitlist for clients it considers a good fit.

pillars.title: Empower Recovery: support while you live at home
pillars.body: Empower Recovery is the centre's answer for people who need real structure around substance use but cannot or do not want to leave home for a residential program. It is non-residential and does not follow the 12 steps. Clients work with a counsellor and a recovery coach, family can be brought in when that helps, and EXOMind sessions may be added if the team thinks they fit. The centre is upfront about the limits: anyone who needs medically supervised withdrawal, round-the-clock care or psychiatric stabilization is pointed to a higher level of care first.

pillars.title: Helping families open the door
pillars.body: A lot of the first calls come from worried relatives. The centre's Pathways to Reconnection service works with a family before, during and after a hard conversation, and it avoids the ambush style of intervention. Ryan Snow is an ARISE-trained interventionist, which is an invitational model built around the family. Sue Snow brings her own experience as a mother of people in recovery. Once someone is in care, Pathways to Wholeness gives continuing support, with counselling, relapse prevention and group connection.

pillars.title: A heritage house in Currie, with body care on site
pillars.body: The centre is in Brad House, a white two-storey heritage building in Currie near Mount Royal University, a short drive from downtown Calgary along Crowchild Trail. Inside are counselling rooms, a salt room called the Siwa Sanctuary and treatment rooms used by an acupuncturist and a registered massage therapist. The centre runs workshops and substance-free gatherings here, and Google reviewers mention sound baths and women's circles. Parking is on site.

overviewH2: How care works at the Centre for Wholeness & Well Being
overview: Everyone starts with a free consultation. The centre says you do not need to know what you need before you call, and the point of the first conversation is to work out which pathway makes sense. From there the team builds an individual plan instead of placing people into a fixed program, so the length and mix of sessions vary from person to person.

The plan can draw on counselling, recovery coaching, family work and what the centre calls nervous system restoration: Neuro Rebalancing, acupuncture, massage and Reiki. Its recovery.com profile lists talk therapies including CBT, DBT, ACT and Internal Family Systems, along with group and family therapy. The centre also offers one-to-one psychedelic integration coaching for people who have had, or are considering, a psychedelic experience. It describes this as harm reduction and states that it does not provide substances.
serviceCaption: 12 services · as described on the centre's website
afterOverview: Fees for counselling and coaching are not listed anywhere public. The centre says it keeps pricing flexible so more people can afford care, and it covers costs in the free consult. Clients can claim sessions through workplace health benefits, and the centre partners with Beautifi for monthly financing on services over $1,000. As a registered charity it also takes donations and issues tax receipts for them.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is the Centre for Wholeness & Well Being a residential rehab?
faqs.a: No. It is an outpatient counselling and recovery centre in southwest Calgary, and clients go home after each appointment. There are no beds, no detox and no 24-hour care. The centre says that if someone needs medically supervised withdrawal, a safer place to stay or psychiatric stabilization, residential or hospital care is the better fit, and it will tell you so.

faqs.q: What is the Empower Recovery program?
faqs.a: Empower Recovery is the centre's non-residential, non-12-step recovery program for people dealing with substance use. It combines counselling, recovery coaching and family support, with EXOMind sessions added when the team thinks they are appropriate. It suits people who want more structure than occasional counselling but cannot step away from work or family, and people stepping down from a residential program.

faqs.q: How much does it cost, and can I use my benefits?
faqs.a: The centre does not publish its fees. It says pricing for counselling and coaching is flexible and is discussed during a free first consultation. Receipts are provided so you can claim through a health benefits plan, and its recovery.com profile lists plans including Manulife, Sun Life, Medavie Blue Cross, Green Shield, Empire Life and Industrial Alliance. Monthly financing through Beautifi is available for services over $1,000.

No. The Centre for Wholeness & Well Being does not provide medical detox or medically supervised withdrawal. If you need to stop drinking or using safely under medical care, start with your doctor, a hospital or a Recovery Alberta detox service, then look at outpatient support here afterwards.

faqs.q: What is EXOMind, and how does the centre use it?
faqs.a: EXOMind is a neurostimulation device that the centre describes as non-invasive, Health Canada-cleared and based on TMS (transcranial magnetic stimulation). The centre says it uses EXOMind as one part of a care plan alongside counselling and recovery support, not as a stand-alone treatment, and that a course is often about six sessions, though plans vary. Ask at your consultation whether it suits you.

faqs.q: Can families get help if a loved one is not ready?
faqs.a: Yes. The centre's Pathways to Reconnection service helps families prepare for a difficult conversation and invite a loved one into care without pressure or confrontation. Family members can also book counselling for themselves, and family involvement is built into the Empower Recovery program when it helps.

faqs.q: Who runs the Centre for Wholeness & Well Being?
faqs.a: It was co-founded by Ryan Snow and Sue Snow, who are both counsellors there. Ryan is a certified addiction counsellor, recovery coach and ARISE-trained interventionist, and Sue holds a B.A. and M.Ed. with credentials including CCDC and MPCC. The centre is operated by the Alberta Association for Better Communities, a registered charity.

faqs.q: Where is the centre and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is in Brad House at 3911 Trasimene Crescent SW in Currie, Calgary (T3E 7J6), about 10 to 15 minutes by car from downtown. Google Maps lists the street as Trasimeno Crescent, but it is the same place. The centre suggests driving north on Quesnay Wood Drive SW, turning left on Normandy Drive, left on Alexandria and then left onto Trasimene. Parking is on site.

According to its Google listing, the centre is open Monday to Friday from 10am to 8pm and Saturday from 10am to noon, and closed on Sundays. Evening appointments make it easier to fit sessions around a work day. Call (825) 413-3100 or email hello@cfwwyyc.com to book.

faqs.q: Is the centre only for addiction recovery?
faqs.a: No. Many clients come for anxiety, burnout, grief, trauma, stress or a major life change, and some come for acupuncture or massage therapy alone. Addiction recovery and family support make up one of several pathways the centre offers.
